newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Sulzer says 1996 net profit 82 mln Sfr.
newsitem.headline: Sulzer says 1996 net profit 82 mln Sfr.

text.p: Swiss engineering group Sulzer AG said that its 1996 net profit was 82 million Swiss francs, down from 92 million in 1995.
It also proposed holding its dividend steady at 12 francs per registered share and participation certificate.
It said that it will create a unitary share, by transforming its participation certificates into registered shares.
It also proposed stipulating a uniform limit of five percent for registration and voting rights, Sulzer said in a statement.
Further, it said that it would reduce the number of its board members.

"Within the framework of the dual corporate strategy -- division into medical technology and industrial activities -- a realignment of the Sulzer Board of Directors is planned which will result in a reduction in the number of Board members," Sulzer said.
It said that Raymond Cornaz, Mathis Cabiallavetta and Rudolf Hug have declined to be re-elected. The board members Peter Plaelti, Urs Buehler and Reto Domeniconi will stand for re-election, it said.

On January 29 Sulzer had denied rumours circulating in the Swiss share market about plans to simplify its share structure. However, a spokesman had also said that a change in the share structure was always something that was being evaluated ahead of shareholders' meetings.
Sulzer did not give an outlook for the current year, but last month it said the outlook for 1997 was positive.
Sulzer has often cautioned that its 1996 net profit would be lower than in 1995 due to restructuring charges and extraordinary expenses.
Sulzer will also adopt International Accounting Standards (IAS) in its 1996 accounts, which includes a revaluation of land and buildings according to the standard of acquisition values.

Sulzer had predicted a higher net profit for 1996 until September. But then a U.S. appeals court judgement in another patent dispute forced Sulzer to pay Stryker Corp $73 million, twice what Sulzer had set aside in provisions for the case, resulting in an added 1996 charge of 45 million Swiss francs.
The the other factor dragging down 1996 profits was provisions and losses at weaving machinery unit Sulzer Rueti, whose 1995 loss of 35 million Swiss francs was expected to at least double this year.
Rueti will also take a charge of up to 36 million Swiss francs this year for a program to cut 950 of its 3,600 jobs by end-1997 and reorganise production.
